REA and Reverse Engineering Oct 14, 2026 
REA has turned reverse engineering into an everyday task for AI agents. Drawing on conversations with reverse engineers in the security industry, a look at how software protection, cracking and cloning, and this reverse engineering craze might change once the barrier is gone. 
A rooftop in Dali. Sep 7, 2026 
An avatar may be a tiny image, but behind it are a relationship, a memory from a trip, and a game we both love. That means more to me than the image itself. 
When AI Misunderstands Aug 28, 2026 
Starting with whether someone can ever truly understand "red," I found myself wondering why AI so often fails to understand "that earlier one." Language may work less like a container and more like an index into experience, while project work depends on a history that others can pick up and continue. 
README? LandingPage Aug 25, 2026 
On how to write a good README. 
Badminton Singles Aug 5, 2026 
I played singles twice recently. Compared to doubles, it is much more physically demanding, and the court feels bigger... 
Network Proxy Issues Jul 14, 2026 
After switching proxy clients, GitHub, YouTube, and ChatGPT web pages all work, but Codex can't connect. The issue lies in system proxy, process environment, and command-line networking being different layers. 
MIT Licenses Code, Not the Whole Product Jun 11, 2026 
A discussion on open source issues sparked by a derivative work of Mole, along with reflections on how AI lowering the barrier to coding impacts open source. 
Moving My Blog to Astro Apr 14, 2026 
Switching from Next.js to Astro. 
After Listening to "The Economics of Exhaustion" Mar 30, 2026 
Yesterday I listened to Episode E227 of the podcast 知行小酒馆, titled "The Economics of Exhaustion: Why has technology advanced, yet we feel more tired?" The content of this episode happened to resonate with my recent sense of fatigue.

I thought I could keep learning as I age, but I just can't keep up, not at all...

About 
Hi, Aries here 👋 
I’ve been an engineer for over nine years. I used to work on data security in the video conferencing industry; these days I mainly work on open-source private cloud storage. 
My interests are a bit of a mix. I build tools for myself in my spare time and share them publicly. I’m exploring ways to live, hobbies, products, and approaches to AI that interest me. I believe AI will make the world a better place. 
My ideas usually start as complaints about everyday annoyances: long X Articles without a table of contents, browser bookmarks that pile up and barely get used, or half an hour in the store dashboard uploading assets and checking listings and privacy details whenever an extension release needs an asset update. 
With AI’s help, I can build small tools to deal with these problems without being held back by limited energy, the tech stacks I know, or complicated development docs. Thank you, AI. 
These tools mostly solve my own problems and fit my own habits. They don’t have much broader appeal, so they don’t have many users (or so I keep telling myself). I’ve started releasing them publicly and keeping them updated, hoping more people will find them useful. 
I write down thoughts, experiences, and whatever else is on my mind here. If you’re into games, anime, or badminton too, and hate AI slop, clickbait, and shouty slogans, maybe we could be friends. 
If you’ve got a good idea and need an engineer, get in touch. 
Dad to a boy · staff to two cats · love my wife · into games and anime · badminton
